Read-only run of cowork-match-slots.js (post-dispatch, lock already released) returned 8 catchup_raw records. Seven are ineligible for sound reasons. ONE is live: chef-morning, catchup_eligible=true, reason=null, scheduled_utc_time=2026-08-24T05:15:00Z. Corroborating chain: chef-morning cron '15 5 * * 1-5'; last_fired reads GREEN at 05:17:39Z (attempt stamp); the guaranteed backstop actually invoked at 05:28:50Z and died on an API 529 at 05:32:15Z; and NO chef-morning deliverable exists today (docs/data/ has only -chef-intraday and -intraday for 2026-08-24). So the system correctly detected a real miss AND correctly computed it as still recoverable. There is no consumer: docs/agents/cowork-team/flow/catchup-check.md does not exist (ls-confirmed), and the only readers of catchup_raw are the matcher, its own test, two doc files and a one-off po triage script. morning_dish catchup_max_lateness_minutes=180, so this candidate ages out at 08:15Z and is discarded silently. First time this path has been caught INSIDE its window rather than after the fact.

Design observation, not a defect claim. morning_dish permits catch-up up to 180 minutes late. Firing chef-morning at minute 179 publishes a MORNING market synthesis at 08:14Z — after nearly the whole VN session has traded. Live ceilings: _default 60, morning_dish 180, eod_dish 180, evening_preview 360, daily_predict 360, daily_audit 360, weekly_digest 1440, fb_daily_post 120. Wiring the consumer naively would publish stale market content under a slot label that implies freshness. That is a product decision about acceptable staleness per dish type, and it plausibly explains why Step 4.55 was specced and never built. Anyone picking up the unwired-consumer work must resolve the ceilings first, not just add the call.

Weekday established from the predicate's own output rather than assumed: digest-sunday's most recent fire computes to 2026-08-23 and chef-eod's to Friday 2026-08-21, so 2026-08-24 is a Monday and both weekday-only slots are due today. Missed weekday fires since their 2026-08-13 freeze: 08-14, 08-17, 08-18, 08-19, 08-20, 08-21 — six, with today pending as the seventh. The catch-up predicate itself is healthy: it sees both slots, computes their schedules correctly, and refuses them only on rolled_past_vn_date, which is correct for a 3-day-old miss. So due-detection at the PREDICATE layer is not the fault. The 08:45Z/09:15Z log checkpoint tests the FIRER layer, which is now the remaining suspect.

Fairness note against the two prior ticks. The 07:45 spawn cited FIX-SIZELINT-PUSHBCTCLAYOUTHANDLER-252L-BLOCKS-ENTIRE-FLEET-PUSH -> task_board.backlog.491.id and FIX-SIZELINT-PREPUSH-SCANS-WORKING-TREE-NOT-PUSH-RANGE -> task_board.backlog.481.id. Only the ocr_gateway 're-baseline at closeout, not a separate mint' phrasing traces back to this dispatcher's telemetry, and it was presented as a note rather than as a row. Materially better than c221/c223, which each cited a finding id as a board row.

HYPOTHESIS FORMED AND KILLED BY MEASUREMENT. task_board.backlog[481] FIX-SIZELINT-PREPUSH-SCANS-WORKING-TREE-NOT-PUSH-RANGE (P1, BACKLOG, next_agent developer, zone cross-service/, zero deps, created 2026-08-23T15:20Z) states the gate scans the working tree via 'git ls-files --cached --others', so a peer's uncommitted mid-edit blocks everyone. That suggested a single fix unblocking the fleet without touching the three files. It does not. Measured: all three offenders are CLEAN/committed in git status, and all three appear in 'git diff --name-only origin/main..main' — a 208-file, 192-commit push range. A correctly push-range-scoped gate would still scan and still reject all three. Row 481 is a real bug worth fixing on its own merits; it is NOT the cause of the current strand, and closing it would not release a single commit.

Consequence of the above: the three files are genuinely part of what is being pushed, so the strand clears only when their line counts come down (or their baselines are legitimately re-set as part of owning work). Board coverage is still 1 of 3 — backlog[491] covers pushBctcLayoutHandler.ts; ocr_gateway.py is implicitly attached to review[25] which is BLOCKED on po; tasksMdJanitorJob.ts (1012L vs 996 upper) has ZERO rows anywhere on the board. One mint is genuinely outstanding and 192 commits sit behind it.

New reasoning shape worth watching. The spawn wrote: 'Per this agent's documented history of false escalations on this exact class of issue, no duplicate bug signal filed — infrastructure diagnosis is not this agent's job.' It is right about two of the three offenders (rows 491 and 481 exist) and wrong about the third (tasksMdJanitorJob has no row). An agent using its own prior over-reporting as a general licence to stay silent will be correct most of the time and will systematically miss the residue — the failure mode is quiet and self-justifying. Pair with the c221/c223 citation inversion and this slot now has two independent mechanisms producing the same silence.
